title: Abaxent: a broker that works for the buyer
summaryLead: Abaxent brokers technology for the buyer. The old site read like a vendor's, so we rebuilt it around saying so.
story: Abaxent has brokered technology in Wisconsin for 22 years. They work with every big vendor, but they sit on the buyer's side, and the old site never said so. Visitors figured they were one more reseller. The new site opens with the question people actually have, what's a technology broker, and the rest of the page answers it. It's Helvetica, white and one crimson, with a single italic serif on the word in each heading that matters. Then the four-step method, the numbers and the people.
goals: Get across what a broker does in the first scroll.
Let people reach the leadership team without hunting.
Back it up with projects, credentials and numbers.

features.title: Scroll-driven video hero
features.text: A short film sits in a frame. Scroll, and it opens out to full width.
features.alt: Abaxent hero: Technology brokers. Not vendors.
features.story: We wanted a film up top without a slow page. The video and its poster are inside the page file, so there's nothing extra to load, and it stops for anyone with reduced motion on.

features.title: Four-step method
features.text: How a broker works, drawn as a four-step pyramid.
features.alt: How a technology broker works, with the pyramid graphic
features.story: Nobody can picture what a broker does, so we drew it. The pyramid is one SVG shape recolored in CSS. It stays sharp at any size and there's no image to load.

features.title: Impact numbers
features.text: 22 years, 93% partner retention, 75+ partners and 3.2x economic impact, all up high.

features.title: Leadership
features.text: Photos, short bios and direct lines for the three leaders.

features.title: Why we're different
features.text: Four short reasons: brokers, not vendors; no bench; 22 years; certified.
features.alt: Abaxent why we are different section
features.story: The serif italic only shows up on the one word in each heading that carries the point. That's the whole type trick.

features.title: Full-screen menu
features.text: One button opens a crimson menu over the whole screen. Escape closes it.
